description: ProofForge Radical Categorical Curriculum — Levels 3 through 12. Each level = subcategory closed under morphism composition. Difficulty = categorical depth, not proof length.
design_principle: Level L theorems genuinely require tactics from the Level L subcategory and cannot be solved by lower-level tactics alone. Custom recursive definitions prevent simp/omega monoculture at Level 4+. Classical axioms required at Level 5+.

categorical_framework.level_4: Initial algebras: induction (recursive reasoning on Nat, List)
categorical_framework.level_9: 2-morphisms: conv, simp only, targeted rw (controlled rewriting)

definitions:
-- Custom recursive definitions for Level 4+ theorems.
-- The training pipeline MUST load these into the Lean REPL
-- before checking any Level 4+ theorem.

def myDouble : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | n + 1 => myDouble n + 2

def myPow2 : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 1
  | n + 1 => 2 * myPow2 n

def myLen {α : Type _} : List α → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | _ :: xs => 1 + myLen xs

def myApp {α : Type _} : List α → List α → List α
  | [], ys => ys
  | x :: xs, ys => x :: myApp xs ys

def myRev {α : Type _} : List α → List α
  | [] => []
  | x :: xs => myApp (myRev xs) [x]

def myMap {α β : Type _} (f : α → β) : List α → List β
  | [] => []
  | x :: xs => f x :: myMap f xs

def myFilter {α : Type _} (p : α → Bool) : List α → List α
  | [] => []
  | x :: xs => if p x then x :: myFilter p xs else myFilter p xs

def myAll {α : Type _} (p : α → Bool) : List α → Bool
  | [] => true
  | x :: xs => p x && myAll p xs

def myIter {α : Type _} (f : α → α) : Nat → α → α
  | 0, x => x
  | n + 1, x => f (myIter f n x)

tiers.name: level_3_coproducts
tiers.description: Cases / Coproducts — Eliminate disjunctions and type constructors via case analysis. The universal property of the coproduct: to map out of C₁ + C₂, handle each injection separately.

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_01 (p q : Prop) : p ∨ q → q ∨ p := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h; cases h with
| inl hp => right; exact hp
| inr hq => left; exact hq

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_02 (p q r : Prop) : p ∨ q → (p → r) → (q → r) → r := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h hpr hqr; cases h with
| inl hp => exact hpr hp
| inr hq => exact hqr hq

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_03 (p q r : Prop) : p ∧ (q ∨ r) → (p ∧ q) ∨ (p ∧ r) := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro ⟨hp, hqr⟩; cases hqr with
| inl hq => left; exact ⟨hp, hq⟩
| inr hr => right; exact ⟨hp, hr⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_04 (p q r : Prop) : (p ∨ q) ∨ r → p ∨ (q ∨ r) := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h; cases h with
| inl hpq =>
  cases hpq with
  | inl hp => left; exact hp
  | inr hq => right; left; exact hq
| inr hr => right; right; exact hr

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_05 (p q r : Prop) : p ∨ (q ∨ r) → (p ∨ q) ∨ r := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h; cases h with
| inl hp => left; left; exact hp
| inr hqr =>
  cases hqr with
  | inl hq => left; right; exact hq
  | inr hr => right; exact hr

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_06 (p q : Prop) : p ∨ q → ¬p → q := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h hnp; cases h with
| inl hp => exact absurd hp hnp
| inr hq => exact hq

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_07 (p q : Prop) : p ∨ q → ¬q → p := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h hnq; cases h with
| inl hp => exact hp
| inr hq => exact absurd hq hnq

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_08 (p q r s : Prop) : (p → r) → (q → s) → p ∨ q → r ∨ s := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro hpr hqs h; cases h with
| inl hp => left; exact hpr hp
| inr hq => right; exact hqs hq

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_09 (p q : Prop) : ¬p ∧ ¬q → ¬(p ∨ q) := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro ⟨hnp, hnq⟩ h; cases h with
| inl hp => exact hnp hp
| inr hq => exact hnq hq

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_10 (p q r : Prop) : (p ∨ q) ∧ (p ∨ r) → p ∨ (q ∧ r) := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro ⟨hpq, hpr⟩; cases hpq with
| inl hp => left; exact hp
| inr hq =>
  cases hpr with
  | inl hp => left; exact hp
  | inr hr => right; exact ⟨hq, hr⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_11 (n : Nat) : n = 0 ∨ ∃ m, n = m + 1 := by
theorems.known_proof:
cases n with
| zero => left; rfl
| succ m => right; exact ⟨m, rfl⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_12 (n : Nat) : n = 0 ∨ 0 < n := by
theorems.known_proof:
cases n with
| zero => left; rfl
| succ m => right; omega

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_13 (b : Bool) : b = true ∨ b = false := by
theorems.known_proof:
cases b with
| true => left; rfl
| false => right; rfl

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_14 {α : Type*} (o : Option α) : o = none ∨ ∃ a, o = some a := by
theorems.known_proof:
cases o with
| none => left; rfl
| some a => right; exact ⟨a, rfl⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_15 (n : Nat) : n ≠ 0 → ∃ m, n = m + 1 := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h; cases n with
| zero => exact absurd rfl h
| succ m => exact ⟨m, rfl⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_16 (p q r : Prop) : (p ∧ q) ∨ (p ∧ r) → p := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h; cases h with
| inl hpq => exact hpq.1
| inr hpr => exact hpr.1

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_17 (p : Prop) : p ∨ p → p := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h; cases h with
| inl hp => exact hp
| inr hp => exact hp

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l3_18 (p q : Prop) : (p ∨ q) → (¬p ∨ ¬q) → (p ∧ ¬q) ∨ (¬p ∧ q) := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro hpq hnpnq
cases hpq with
| inl hp =>
  cases hnpnq with
  | inl hnp => exact absurd hp hnp
  | inr hnq => left; exact ⟨hp, hnq⟩
| inr hq =>
  cases hnpnq with
  | inl hnp => right; exact ⟨hnp, hq⟩
  | inr hnq => exact absurd hq hnq

tiers.name: level_4_initial_algebras
tiers.description: Induction / Initial Algebras — Prove properties of recursively defined functions by structural induction. The unique morphism from the initial algebra (Nat, List) to any algebra with matching structure.

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l4_01 : ∀ n, myDouble n = 2 * n := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro n
induction n with
| zero => rfl
| succ n ih => simp [myDouble, ih]; omega

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l4_02 : ∀ n, 0 < myPow2 n := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro n
induction n with
| zero => simp [myPow2]
| succ n ih => simp [myPow2]; omega

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l4_03 {α : Type*} (xs : List α) : myApp xs [] = xs := by
theorems.known_proof:
induction xs with
| nil => rfl
| cons x xs ih => simp [myApp, ih]

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l4_04 {α : Type*} (xs ys zs : List α) : myApp (myApp xs ys) zs = myApp xs (myApp ys zs) := by
theorems.known_proof:
induction xs with
| nil => simp [myApp]
| cons x xs ih => simp [myApp, ih]

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l4_05 {α : Type*} (xs ys : List α) : myLen (myApp xs ys) = myLen xs + myLen ys := by
theorems.known_proof:
induction xs with
| nil => simp [myApp, myLen]
| cons x xs ih => simp [myApp, myLen, ih]; omega

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l4_06 : ∀ n m, myDouble (n + m) = myDouble n + myDouble m := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro n m
induction n with
| zero => simp [myDouble]
| succ n ih => simp [myDouble, ih]; omega

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l4_07 {α β : Type*} (f : α → β) (xs : List α) : myLen (myMap f xs) = myLen xs := by
theorems.known_proof:
induction xs with
| nil => simp [myMap, myLen]
| cons x xs ih => simp [myMap, myLen, ih]

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l4_08 {α : Type*} (xs : List α) : myMap id xs = xs := by
theorems.known_proof:
induction xs with
| nil => simp [myMap]
| cons x xs ih => simp [myMap, ih]

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l4_09 {α β γ : Type*} (f : β → γ) (g : α → β) (xs : List α) : myMap f (myMap g xs) = myMap (f ∘ g) xs := by
theorems.known_proof:
induction xs with
| nil => simp [myMap]
| cons x xs ih => simp [myMap, Function.comp, ih]

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l4_10 {α β : Type*} (f : α → β) (xs ys : List α) : myMap f (myApp xs ys) = myApp (myMap f xs) (myMap f ys) := by
theorems.known_proof:
induction xs with
| nil => simp [myApp, myMap]
| cons x xs ih => simp [myApp, myMap, ih]

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l4_11 {α : Type*} (p : α → Bool) (xs : List α) : myLen (myFilter p xs) ≤ myLen xs := by
theorems.known_proof:
induction xs with
| nil => simp [myFilter, myLen]
| cons x xs ih =>
  simp only [myFilter]
  split
  · simp [myLen]; omega
  · simp [myLen]; omega

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l4_12 {α : Type*} (xs : List α) : myAll (fun _ => true) xs = true := by
theorems.known_proof:
induction xs with
| nil => rfl
| cons x xs ih => simp [myAll, ih]

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l4_13 : ∀ n, n ≤ myDouble n := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro n
induction n with
| zero => simp [myDouble]
| succ n ih => simp [myDouble]; omega

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l4_14 {α : Type*} (p : α → Bool) (xs ys : List α) : myFilter p (myApp xs ys) = myApp (myFilter p xs) (myFilter p ys) := by
theorems.known_proof:
induction xs with
| nil => simp [myApp, myFilter]
| cons x xs ih =>
  simp only [myApp, myFilter]
  split
  · simp [myApp, ih]
  · exact ih

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l4_15 {α : Type*} (xs : List α) : myApp [] xs = xs := by
theorems.known_proof: simp [myApp]

tiers.name: level_5_exponentials
tiers.description: Classical Logic / Exponentials — Proof by contradiction, excluded middle, De Morgan's laws (classical direction). Exponential objects in category theory: function spaces, negation as the exponential A → ⊥.

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l5_01 (p : Prop) : ¬¬p → p := by
theorems.known_proof: intro h; by_contra hn; exact h hn

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l5_02 (p q : Prop) : (¬q → ¬p) → p → q := by
theorems.known_proof: intro h hp; by_contra hnq; exact h hnq hp

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l5_03 (p q : Prop) : ¬(p ∧ q) → ¬p ∨ ¬q := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h
cases Classical.em p with
| inl hp => right; intro hq; exact h ⟨hp, hq⟩
| inr hnp => left; exact hnp

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l5_04 (p : Prop) : p ∨ ¬p := by
theorems.known_proof: exact Classical.em p

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l5_05 (p q : Prop) : ((p → q) → p) → p := by
theorems.known_proof: intro h; by_contra hnp; exact hnp (h (fun hp => absurd hp hnp))

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l5_06 (p q : Prop) : ¬(p → q) → p ∧ ¬q := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h
constructor
· by_contra hnp; exact h (fun hp => absurd hp hnp)
· intro hq; exact h (fun _ => hq)

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l5_07 (p q : Prop) : (p → q) → (¬p ∨ q) := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h
cases Classical.em p with
| inl hp => right; exact h hp
| inr hnp => left; exact hnp

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l5_08 {α : Type*} (p : α → Prop) : ¬(∀ x, p x) → ∃ x, ¬p x := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h
by_contra hn
apply h
intro x
by_contra hnpx
exact hn ⟨x, hnpx⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l5_09 (p q : Prop) : ¬(p ∧ q) ↔ ¬p ∨ ¬q := by
theorems.known_proof:
constructor
· intro h
  cases Classical.em p with
  | inl hp => right; intro hq; exact h ⟨hp, hq⟩
  | inr hnp => left; exact hnp
· intro h ⟨hp, hq⟩
  cases h with
  | inl hnp => exact hnp hp
  | inr hnq => exact hnq hq

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l5_10 (p q : Prop) : (p → q) ∨ (q → p) := by
theorems.known_proof:
cases Classical.em p with
| inl hp =>
  cases Classical.em q with
  | inl hq => left; intro _; exact hq
  | inr hnq => right; intro hq; exact absurd hq hnq
| inr hnp => left; intro hp; exact absurd hp hnp

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l5_11 (p q r : Prop) : (p → q ∨ r) → (p → q) ∨ (p → r) := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h
cases Classical.em p with
| inl hp =>
  cases h hp with
  | inl hq => left; intro _; exact hq
  | inr hr => right; intro _; exact hr
| inr hnp => left; intro hp; exact absurd hp hnp

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l5_12 (p : Prop) : p ↔ ¬¬p := by
theorems.known_proof:
constructor
· intro hp hn; exact hn hp
· intro h; by_contra hn; exact h hn

tiers.name: level_6_composition
tiers.description: Composition — Intermediate objects via have/suffices, equational chains via calc, partial application via apply. Morphism composition in the proof category: A → B → C requires constructing the intermediate object B.

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l6_01 (p q r : Prop) : (p ↔ q) → (q ↔ r) → (p ↔ r) := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro hpq hqr
constructor
· intro hp
  have hq := hpq.mp hp
  exact hqr.mp hq
· intro hr
  have hq := hqr.mpr hr
  exact hpq.mpr hq

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l6_02 (p q r s : Prop) : (p → q) → (q → r) → (r → s) → p → s := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro hpq hqr hrs hp
have hq := hpq hp
have hr := hqr hq
exact hrs hr

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l6_03 (p q r s : Prop) : (p ↔ r) → (q ↔ s) → (p ∧ q ↔ r ∧ s) := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro hpr hqs
constructor
· intro ⟨hp, hq⟩
  have hr := hpr.mp hp
  have hs := hqs.mp hq
  exact ⟨hr, hs⟩
· intro ⟨hr, hs⟩
  have hp := hpr.mpr hr
  have hq := hqs.mpr hs
  exact ⟨hp, hq⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l6_04 (p q r s : Prop) : (p ↔ r) → (q ↔ s) → (p ∨ q ↔ r ∨ s) := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro hpr hqs
constructor
· intro h; cases h with
  | inl hp => left; exact hpr.mp hp
  | inr hq => right; exact hqs.mp hq
· intro h; cases h with
  | inl hr => left; exact hpr.mpr hr
  | inr hs => right; exact hqs.mpr hs

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l6_05 (a b : Nat) : a ≤ b → a * a ≤ b * b := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h
have h1 : a * a ≤ a * b := Nat.mul_le_mul_left a h
have h2 : a * b ≤ b * b := Nat.mul_le_mul_right b h
exact Nat.le_trans h1 h2

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l6_06 (a b c : Nat) : a * b * c = c * b * a := by
theorems.known_proof:
calc a * b * c
    = c * (a * b) := by rw [Nat.mul_comm (a * b) c]
  _ = c * (b * a) := by rw [Nat.mul_comm a b]
  _ = c * b * a := by rw [Nat.mul_assoc]

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l6_07 {α : Type*} (p q : α → Prop) : (∀ x, p x → q x) → (∃ x, p x) → ∃ x, q x := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h ⟨x, hpx⟩
have hqx := h x hpx
exact ⟨x, hqx⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l6_08 (p q : Prop) : (p ↔ q) → (¬p ↔ ¬q) := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro hpq
constructor
· intro hnp hq
  have hp := hpq.mpr hq
  exact hnp hp
· intro hnq hp
  have hq := hpq.mp hp
  exact hnq hq

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l6_09 {α : Type*} (xs ys : List α) : myLen xs ≤ myLen (myApp xs ys) := by
theorems.known_proof:
have h : myLen (myApp xs ys) = myLen xs + myLen ys := by
  induction xs with
  | nil => simp [myApp, myLen]
  | cons x xs ih => simp [myApp, myLen, ih]; omega
rw [h]
omega

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l6_10 (a b c : Nat) : a + b + c = c + b + a := by
theorems.known_proof:
calc a + b + c
    = (a + b) + c := rfl
  _ = c + (a + b) := by rw [Nat.add_comm]
  _ = c + (b + a) := by rw [Nat.add_comm a b]
  _ = c + b + a := by rw [Nat.add_assoc]

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l6_11 (p q r : Prop) : (p → q) → (q → r) → p → r := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro hpq hqr hp
suffices hq : q from hqr hq
exact hpq hp

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l6_12 (a b : Nat) : a ≤ b → a * a ≤ a * b ∧ a * b ≤ b * b := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h
constructor
· exact Nat.mul_le_mul_left a h
· exact Nat.mul_le_mul_right b h

tiers.name: level_7_universal_properties
tiers.description: Universal Properties — Witness construction via use/constructor/exact ⟨...⟩. To inhabit an existential ∃x, P(x), you must provide a concrete witness x and prove P(x). The defining property of coproducts and products in type theory.

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l7_01 : ∀ n : Nat, ∃ m : Nat, m > n := by
theorems.known_proof: intro n; exact ⟨n + 1, by omega⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l7_02 : ∀ n : Nat, ∃ m, n + m = 2 * n := by
theorems.known_proof: intro n; exact ⟨n, by omega⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l7_03 : ∀ n : Nat, ∃ m, n = 2 * m ∨ n = 2 * m + 1 := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro n
induction n with
| zero => exact ⟨0, Or.inl (by omega)⟩
| succ n ih =>
  have ⟨m, hm⟩ := ih
  cases hm with
  | inl h => exact ⟨m, Or.inr (by omega)⟩
  | inr h => exact ⟨m + 1, Or.inl (by omega)⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l7_04 {α : Type*} (p : α → Prop) (a : α) : p a → ∃ x, p x := by
theorems.known_proof: intro h; exact ⟨a, h⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l7_05 {α : Type*} : ∃ (f : Nat → Nat), ∀ n, f n > n := by
theorems.known_proof: exact ⟨(· + 1), fun n => by omega⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l7_06 (a b : Nat) : a ≤ b → ∃ d, b = a + d := by
theorems.known_proof: intro h; exact ⟨b - a, by omega⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l7_07 {α : Type*} (p q : α → Prop) : (∃ x, p x ∧ q x) → (∃ x, p x) ∧ (∃ x, q x) := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro ⟨x, hpx, hqx⟩
constructor
· exact ⟨x, hpx⟩
· exact ⟨x, hqx⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l7_08 {α : Type*} (xs : List α) : xs ≠ [] → ∃ a as, xs = a :: as := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h
cases xs with
| nil => exact absurd rfl h
| cons a as => exact ⟨a, as, rfl⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l7_09 {α : Type*} (f : α → β) (xs : List α) : ∃ ys, ys = myMap f xs ∧ myLen ys = myLen xs := by
theorems.known_proof:
exact ⟨myMap f xs, rfl, by
  induction xs with
  | nil => simp [myMap, myLen]
  | cons x xs ih => simp [myMap, myLen, ih]⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l7_10 (n : Nat) : n > 0 → ∃ m, n = m + 1 := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h
cases n with
| zero => omega
| succ m => exact ⟨m, rfl⟩

tiers.name: level_8_natural_transformations
tiers.description: Natural Transformations / Extensionality — Proving equality of functions from pointwise equality (funext), equality of structures from component equality (ext), congruence of function application (congr). In category theory, a natural transformation η: F ⟹ G is determined by its components η_A at each object A.

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l8_01 {α β : Type*} (f g : α → β) : (∀ x, f x = g x) → f = g := by
theorems.known_proof: intro h; funext x; exact h x

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l8_02 {α β : Type*} (f : α → β) : (fun x => f x) = f := by
theorems.known_proof: funext x; rfl

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l8_03 {α β γ : Type*} (f g : α → β) (h : β → γ) : (∀ x, f x = g x) → h ∘ f = h ∘ g := by
theorems.known_proof: intro heq; funext x; simp [Function.comp]; rw [heq x]

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l8_04 {α β γ : Type*} (f g : α → β) (h : γ → α) : (∀ x, f x = g x) → f ∘ h = g ∘ h := by
theorems.known_proof: intro heq; funext x; exact heq (h x)

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l8_05 {α β : Type*} (f : α → β → α) (a₁ a₂ : α) (b₁ b₂ : β) : a₁ = a₂ → b₁ = b₂ → f a₁ b₁ = f a₂ b₂ := by
theorems.known_proof: intro ha hb; congr

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l8_06 {α β : Type*} (p q : α × β) : p.1 = q.1 → p.2 = q.2 → p = q := by
theorems.known_proof: intro h1 h2; exact Prod.ext h1 h2

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l8_07 {α : Type*} : @id α = fun x => x := by
theorems.known_proof: funext x; rfl

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l8_08 {α β γ : Type*} (f : α → β) (g : β → γ) : g ∘ f = fun x => g (f x) := by
theorems.known_proof: funext x; rfl

tiers.name: level_9_2_morphisms
tiers.description: 2-Morphisms / Controlled Rewriting — Targeted rewriting within specific subexpressions using conv, simp only with explicit lemma lists, and computed rw arguments. In category theory, 2-morphisms are morphisms between morphisms — here, transformations of specific parts of a proof term.

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l9_01 (a b c : Nat) : (a + b) * c = a * c + b * c := by
theorems.known_proof: rw [Nat.add_mul]

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l9_02 (a b c : Nat) : a * (b + c) = a * b + a * c := by
theorems.known_proof: rw [Nat.mul_add]

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l9_03 (a b c d : Nat) : (a + b) * (c + d) = a * c + a * d + b * c + b * d := by
theorems.known_proof: rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_add]; omega

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l9_04 (a b : Nat) : (a + b) * (a + b) = a * a + 2 * a * b + b * b := by
theorems.known_proof: rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_add]; omega

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l9_05 {α : Type*} (xs ys : List α) (x : α) : myLen (myApp xs (x :: ys)) = myLen xs + 1 + myLen ys := by
theorems.known_proof:
have h1 : myLen (myApp xs (x :: ys)) = myLen xs + myLen (x :: ys) := by
  induction xs with
  | nil => simp [myApp, myLen]
  | cons a as ih => simp [myApp, myLen, ih]; omega
rw [h1]
simp [myLen]
omega

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l9_06 (a b c : Nat) (h : a = b) : a + c = b + c := by
theorems.known_proof: rw [h]

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l9_07 (a b c : Nat) (h : a = b + c) : 2 * a = 2 * b + 2 * c := by
theorems.known_proof: rw [h, Nat.mul_add]

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l9_08 (f : Nat → Nat) (a b : Nat) (h : a = b) : f a = f b := by
theorems.known_proof: rw [h]

tiers.name: level_10_functors
tiers.description: Functors / Cross-Domain Import — Theorems requiring lemmas from multiple mathematical domains (algebra + order, logic + arithmetic, list + number theory). In category theory, a functor F: C → D maps objects and morphisms between categories, preserving composition. Here, the model must import results from one domain to solve problems in another.

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l10_01 (a b : Nat) : a ∣ b → a ∣ (b + a) := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro ⟨k, hk⟩
exact ⟨k + 1, by rw [hk, Nat.mul_succ]⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l10_02 (a b c : Nat) : a ∣ b → a ∣ c → a ∣ (b + c) := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro ⟨k, hk⟩ ⟨m, hm⟩
exact ⟨k + m, by rw [hk, hm, Nat.mul_add]⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l10_03 (a b c : Nat) : a ∣ b → b ∣ c → a ∣ c := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro ⟨k, hk⟩ ⟨m, hm⟩
exact ⟨k * m, by rw [hm, hk, Nat.mul_assoc]⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l10_04 (a b : Nat) : a ∣ b → a ∣ (b * c) := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro ⟨k, hk⟩
exact ⟨k * c, by rw [hk, Nat.mul_assoc]⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l10_05 (n : Nat) : 2 ∣ (n * (n + 1)) := by
theorems.known_proof:
cases Nat.even_or_odd n with
| inl ⟨k, hk⟩ => exact ⟨k * (n + 1), by rw [hk]; ring⟩
| inr ⟨k, hk⟩ => exact ⟨n * (k + 1), by rw [hk]; ring⟩
theorems.note: May require Mathlib for Nat.even_or_odd and ring

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l10_06 (a b : Nat) (h : a ∣ b) (hb : 0 < b) : a ≤ b := by
theorems.known_proof:
have ⟨k, hk⟩ := h
cases k with
| zero => omega
| succ k => omega

tiers.name: level_11_free_objects
tiers.description: Free Objects / Construction Discovery — The model must invent a mathematical construction (function, set, sequence) as a witness to prove an existential claim. In category theory, free objects are those generated freely by a set of generators — the prover must discover the generators.

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l11_01 : ∃ (f : Nat → Nat), (∀ n, f n > n) ∧ (∀ n, f n < f (n + 1)) := by
theorems.known_proof: exact ⟨(· + 1), fun n => by omega, fun n => by omega⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l11_02 : ∃ (f : Nat → Nat), (∀ n, f (f n) = n) ∧ f ≠ id := by
theorems.known_proof:
exact ⟨fun n => match n with | 0 => 1 | 1 => 0 | n => n,
  fun n => by cases n with | zero => rfl | succ n => cases n with | zero => rfl | succ n => rfl,
  fun h => by have := congr_fun h 0; simp [id] at this⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l11_03 : ∃ (f : Nat → Nat), ∀ n, f n = 0 ∨ f n = 1 := by
theorems.known_proof: exact ⟨fun _ => 0, fun _ => Or.inl rfl⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l11_04 : ∃ (f g : Nat → Nat), (∀ n, f (g n) = n) ∧ (∀ n, g (f n) = n) ∧ f ≠ g := by
theorems.known_proof:
exact ⟨(· + 1), (· - 1),
  fun n => by omega,
  fun n => by omega,
  fun h => by have := congr_fun h 0; simp at this⟩
theorems.note: Nat subtraction: (n+1) - 1 = n but 0 - 1 = 0, so g ∘ f ≠ id on 0. This theorem may need adjustment.

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l11_05 {α : Type*} : ∃ (f : List α → List α), ∀ xs, myLen (f xs) = myLen xs := by
theorems.known_proof: exact ⟨id, fun xs => rfl⟩

tiers.name: level_12_adjunctions
tiers.description: Adjunctions / Strategy Invention — The model must discover a novel proof strategy or combine multiple advanced techniques in an unprecedented way. In category theory, an adjunction F ⊣ G between functors establishes a natural isomorphism Hom(F(A), B) ≅ Hom(A, G(B)) — the model must find the corresponding 'free' and 'forgetful' structure in the proof.

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l12_01 : ∀ n : Nat, ∃ p, p > n ∧ (p % 2 = 1 ∨ p = 2) := by
theorems.known_proof: intro n; exact ⟨2 * n + 3, by omega, Or.inl (by omega)⟩
theorems.note: Simplified version of 'there exists a number > n with a specific property'. Real L12 problems would be competition-math level.

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l12_02 (f : Nat → Nat) (hf : ∀ n, f n ≤ f (n + 1)) (a b : Nat) : a ≤ b → f a ≤ f b := by
theorems.known_proof:
intro h
induction b with
| zero => omega
| succ b ih =>
  cases Nat.eq_or_lt_of_le h with
  | inl heq => rw [heq]
  | inr hlt =>
    have hab : a ≤ b := by omega
    have h1 := ih hab
    exact Nat.le_trans h1 (hf b)

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l12_03 {α : Type*} (f : α → α) (hf : ∀ x, f (f x) = x) : Function.Bijective f := by
theorems.known_proof:
constructor
· intro a b hab
  have : f (f a) = f (f b) := by rw [hab]
  rw [hf, hf] at this
  exact this
· intro b
  exact ⟨f b, hf b⟩

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l12_04 {α : Type*} [Inhabited α] (f : α → α) (hf : Function.Surjective f) : ∃ g : α → α, ∀ x, f (g x) = x := by
theorems.known_proof: exact ⟨fun x => (hf x).choose, fun x => (hf x).choose_spec⟩
theorems.note: Uses axiom of choice via Exists.choose. Requires understanding of Choice in Lean 4.

q_amplifier.description: Every solved theorem at level L can be amplified to generate harder theorems. Four composable amplifiers:

amplifiers.name: q_amplification
amplifiers.description: Replace finite sets with F_q vector spaces. Replace |S| with dim(V). Replace binomial with Gaussian binomial. Requires Mathlib.

amplifiers.name: universalization
amplifiers.description: Replace specific types with universally quantified types. Replace Nat with any ordered semiring. Replace List with any Foldable.

amplifiers.name: witness_compression
amplifiers.description: For existence proofs, require the witness to be minimal/maximal in some ordering. Forces extremal reasoning.

amplifiers.name: kolmogorov_compression
amplifiers.description: Given theorem T with known proof P, prove T with proof length ≤ |P|/2. Engages ProofOptimizer's compression reward.

q_amplifier.fractal_property: Amplifiers compose. q(universalize(compress(T))) at level L produces a theorem at level L+4. A 50-theorem seed generates 200+ theorems.

training_integration.expanding_ring: Use ExpandingRing from curriculum/expanding_ring.py. Each level is a tier. expansion_threshold=0.7, min_tier_steps=20.
training_integration.infrastructure_aware: Use InfrastructureAwareSampler from curriculum/infrastructure_aware.py. required_infra for each theorem = required_tactics field.
training_integration.hard_negative_sampling: ABEL-style: sample problem i with weight (n_i+1)^{-0.5} where n_i = successful proofs so far.
training_integration.phase_amplitude: Amplitude training: pretrain on Mathlib corpus (slow updates). Phase training: online RL on curriculum (fast updates, reset at level transitions).
training_integration.checkpoint_selection: Use ppl@1.4 (temperature-scaled perplexity) from Gloeckle 2023 as cheap convergence signal.
training_integration.diversity_pressure: tactic_usage_fn should return frequency of each tactic. diversity_bonus=2.0 for under-represented tactics (cases, induction, by_contra). monoculture_penalty=0.3 for simp-only proofs.
